title: The Anatomy of the Five Worlds of Darkness and the King Who Rules Them
arc: The teaching maps the proprium as a five-fold cosmos: it traces the five worlds of self-love from their gushing-forth out of the land of darkness, through their kings, bodies, metals, and tastes, up to the composite King of Darkness himself, whose vast outward power is exposed as a confined sense-perception that knows only what stands before its face.
reading:
The chapter is a complete anatomy of self-love. It teaches that what we call hell is not an undifferentiated chaos but an ordered five-fold structure with its own kings, bodies, fruits, and tastes — the negative mirror of the Five Storehouses of divine reception. Everything in this teaching is the proprium described from within its own organization, so that the reader can see the falsity-from-evil exactly as it is built, and recognize where its apparent power ends.

The teaching opens with origin: five "houses" or worlds gushed forth out of the Land of Darkness from the beginning. From these arose five archons, five spirits, five bodies (which are also five tastes), five trees molded, and five kinds of creatures world by world, male and female. This is the proprium generating itself as a complete natural-rational structure — concupiscence (Hyle, the Enthumesis of Death) bringing forth her own perceptions (trees), her own works (fruits/creatures), and her own affections (male/female pairings). Each world has five kings, so the proprium is articulated all the way down: a five-times-five-fold complete structure of self-love, the exact counter-form of the five faculties (mind, thought, teaching, counsel, reflection) in their pure reception.

The middle of the teaching focuses on the smoke-world and on the King of Darkness himself. Smoke is falsity-from-evil obscuring light; its kingship is therefore the ruling principle of confused thought from mingled affection. It rises out of the abyss, the panchōch of all evil, and from this kingship come the wars, the battles of contention, the gates of slaughter — the entire restless aggression of the proprium against the heavens. From the smoke-world the teaching ascends to the lofty kingship of the King of Darkness, whose body is composite: a lion-head (the tyranny of self-love wearing the form of dominion), eagle-shoulders (arrogant high-mindedness), a dragon-belly (sensual-corporeal evil), a fish-tail (natural truth submerged and corrupted in the lowest receptive natural), and limbs in the form of further beasts. His body is gold — but here gold in its opposite sense, the false good of self-love that has usurped the place of celestial good. The bodies of the powers under the smoke-world are likewise gold, and their fruits are lead, the dense weight of falsity in ultimates. Self-love masquerades as celestial good, and the works it actually produces are the lowest natural deadness.

Within him, or within his consort Hyle, are five vehicles: hardness (matter molded by her molder to be unbreakable, that no knife or iron tool can cut — confirmed evil), the mire of concealment in the speech of her members (the deceitful uttering and hearing of folly), her bitterness (the quality of corrupted love), the soul itself held captive within her, and her burning, which scorches like a measure of irons made red-hot in fire — the fire of self-love consuming the Living Soul it has captured. Three further hidden things are within her: her hardness, her shape-shifting concealment in the speech of her members, and her self-painting through the nature of the Land of Darkness — the same image-painting opposed to the Third Ambassador's revealing image. This is Hyle as Enthumesis of Death generating her false likenesses from herself.

The teaching then turns to a striking limitation of the King of Darkness. The gate of those of darkness "knows" — through scent, through sense-perception — every matter sealed up in the mouths of his archons, every signal they give one another. Outwardly he appears omniscient over his domain. But the teaching is precise: their heart is not revealed to him, nor does he reach their mind, their thought, their reflection, their beginning or their end. He knows only by sense-perception what is before his eyes. When he wishes to seize, he spreads out all his limbs; when he is sated, he draws them back into himself, and they fall together like a cloud and a great sphere of iron joined together — the proprium as a clenched, compacted natural mass. His voice is like thunder splitting rocks, and the powers tremble and fall before him like scattered birds. Yet the teaching closes the description with the decisive sentence: he cannot reach what is far from him; he does not see, hear, or know what is far away. Only what is before his face is what he sees and hears and knows. The whole apparent omnipotence of self-love is bounded by sense; it has no interior reach, no penetration into mind or end. This is the critical spiritual lesson: the King of Darkness rules only the sensual-corporeal plane, and possesses no influx into the inner faculties. He can press upon what is in ultimates, but he cannot enter what is interior.

The teaching closes with a clean catalog of the five worlds and their correspondences, which gathers the whole anatomy. The world of Smoke: a body of gold (false good), fruits of lead (dense falsity). The world of Fire: a king with a lion's face (the burning lust of self-love masquerading as zeal), foremost of all wild beasts, body of bronze (corrupt natural good), taste bitter — fire here as common burning fire, lust, opposed to the Living Fire of divine love. The world of Wind: a king with an eagle's face (arrogant intellectual height), body of iron (natural truth in ultimates, but here in its hard fallen form), taste sharp — disordered perception. The world of Water: a king with a fish's face (natural truth wholly submerged in the receptive natural), body of silver (spiritual truth, but corrupted into mere appearance of wisdom), taste sweet — and this sweetness, in its negative sense in this catalog, is the dangerous false sweetness by which the natural mind is seduced when truth is held in mingling. The world of Darkness proper: a king in dragon-form (the proprium as serpentine sensual evil), body of lead and dark-stone (the lowest natural confirmed in the densest falsity), fruit bitter.

The arc of the whole teaching is therefore this: the proprium is not formless. It is a counter-cosmos with its own discrete degrees, its own kings, its own bodies and fruits, its own metals and tastes. To know it as a system is to be able to discriminate it. The teaching exposes its origin (gushing from the Land of Darkness from the beginning), its structure (five worlds with five kings each), its central head (the composite King of Darkness with his five-formed body), its hidden generative power (Hyle with her five vehicles and three concealments), and finally its limit — that all this apparent rule is confined to what stands before the face, with no penetration into heart, mind, thought, reflection, or the beginning and end of any soul. This is why regeneration is possible: the proprium is enormous in ultimates and impotent in the interior. The Lord rules the inmost; the King of Darkness rules only the sense.

major_images.image: Five worlds gushing from the Land of Darkness
major_images.meaning: The proprium articulated into a complete five-fold structure — the negative mirror of the Five Storehouses of divine reception.

major_images.image: King of Darkness with composite beast-body (lion head, eagle shoulders, dragon belly, fish tail) of gold
major_images.meaning: Self-love personified, gathering tyranny, arrogance, sensual evil, and submerged natural truth into one ruling principle whose 'gold' is the false good usurping celestial good.

major_images.image: His limbs spread out and gathered back as a cloud and iron sphere; voice like thunder splitting rocks
major_images.meaning: The clenched compacted force of the proprium in ultimates — vast outward aggression but a closed, hardened mass.

major_images.image: He sees, hears, and knows only what is before his face
major_images.meaning: Self-love is confined to sense-perception in ultimates; it has no influx into heart, mind, thought, reflection, or the beginning and end of the soul.

major_images.image: Five worlds with their metals and tastes (gold/lead, bronze/bitter, iron/sharp, silver/sweet, lead-stone/bitter)
major_images.meaning: Each mode of self-love produces its own corrupt 'good' (metal) and its own actualized work (taste/fruit) — celestial, spiritual, and natural goods all inverted into their proprial counterfeits.

major_images.image: Hyle's five vehicles and three concealments — hardness, mire, bitterness, captive soul, burning fire; deceitful speech, self-painting
major_images.meaning: Concupiscence as the corrupt generative matrix that hardens, conceals, paints false likenesses, and burns the captured Living Soul within itself.
